title: Control flow: sequence, decisions and iteration
goal: Compare sequence, selection and repetition while summing three numbers.

prerequisites.text: You can assign and compare integers; while repetition is introduced below.

sections.title: From the task to an operation
paragraphs: A sequence runs statements in order. A branch selects a path. A loop repeats its body while a condition is true. The example adds 1,2,3: i is the next addend and sum is the sum already processed.

sum = sum + i computes a new sum from the old one. i = i + 1 advances to the next number. <= includes 3; while tests the condition before each iteration, meaning one execution of its body. After processing 3, i becomes 4 and execution stops.

sections.title: Compare sequence, selection and repetition while summing three numbers.
trace: Added 2 to the previous sum of 1.

sections.title: Change one condition and check the prediction
paragraphs: Change the bound from 3 to 4. Predict the additional change to sum.
The first three iterations are unchanged: sum is already 6.

sections.title: When the result differs
paragraphs: Removing the increment keeps the condition true. Do not run an endless experiment: identify the missing step by reading.

sections.title: Now solve your own task
paragraphs: Sum 1 through 5. Write i and sum after every iteration and explain the stopping condition.
Practice contains a separate starter. Predict the result before changing your program. Returning to the example does not replace your source.

selfcheck.prompt: What output follows the specified change? Change the bound from 3 to 4. Predict the additional change to sum.
selfcheck.feedback: The first three iterations are unchanged: sum is already 6. The fourth adds 4: 6+4=10.

selfcheck.prompt: Sum 1 through 5. Write i and sum after every iteration and explain the stopping condition.
selfcheck.feedback: Compare the output with the readable reference case below. Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic. After five iterations, sum is 1, 3, 6, 10, 15; i=6 then ends the loop. Using i<5 instead of i<=5 skips the final term and gives 10 instead of 15.

practice.title: Independent variation
practice.task: Sum 1 through 5. Write i and sum after every iteration and explain the stopping condition.
criteria: Compare the output with the readable reference case below.
Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic.
After five iterations, sum is 1, 3, 6, 10, 15; i=6 then ends the loop. Using i<5 instead of i<=5 skips the final term and gives 10 instead of 15.
practice.hint: The first three iterations are unchanged: sum is already 6. The fourth adds 4: 6+4=10.

steps.action: Sum 1 through 5. Write i and sum after every iteration and explain the stopping condition.
Write your solution in a separate starter; keep your previous work.
Compare actual output with your prediction and explain any difference.

terms.definition: An alternative control path chosen by a condition.
One execution of a loop body.
After k steps, sum includes exactly the processed even values.
